questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard and expensive. Found through airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Gives you the privacy not available through on campus living; but also makes it harder to create a social network.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Took place online. Often required contacting professors directly about specifics.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The guide given to all students on the registration platform.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. Only obstacles were overlapping courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Invest time in planning. Take the opportunity to explore the catalogue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The university I attended (UW) had a numeral structure (100-400) that determined the level of courses. Everything below 300 compared to Danish high school levels and were quite unsatisfying. Everything above 300 compared to Danish university courses, although with more essays and weekly written assignments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less readings; more writings (essays etc.); in-class discussions; professors often reflected upon material in relation to contemporary politics, which often gave the impression of a partiality and lacking objective, critical approach.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Jewish Philosophy. Jewish poetry. MENA Illustrated. Popular Film and The Holocaust. A Tale of Two Cities: Tel Aviv and Jerusalem. Supervised Study with Translation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Philosophy courses.

questions.answer: Price of certain goods.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Was given free public transport as included in the program. Social events like concerts were often free or at a very low price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A few events took place for international students the first few weeks. During the semester there was an active program of talks, concerts, exhibitions etc. available for all students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Exploring the city. Finding a social group and integrate into their daily lives with everything included (partying, hiking, playing sports etc.)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Night life. Hiking. Sports. Cultural events.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Rather easy; American students find foreigners exciting and very interested in showing you their way of life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Really just approach someone that seems interesting (e.g. in class) and there is a high chance they will welcome you into their friend group.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Age difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hospitality.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to enjoy both the urban sites and the sorrounding natural areas as these are easily available. Cross your social boundaries and make an effort to establish a social circle. Enjoy the on-campus facilities (IMA, concert halls etc.)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and socialize among American students rather than other exchange students if possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Got to experience American university life with everything included.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Crossing social boundaries and creating a social network. The first couple of weeks/month can be very lonely.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
